name: Biocon Ltd
title: Biocon Ltd - 532523 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Biocon Q1 FY27 shows generics margin recovery to 7% and biosimilars EBITDA at 25%, but Syngene revenue fell 16% and working capital and net debt rose ~INR1,100 crores on inventory build for H2 launches.

summary.headline: Biocon Q1 FY27 group revenue up 10% YoY with EBITDA of INR902 crore (21% margin); biosimilars and generics grew while Syngene fell 16%.
summary.overview: Group operating revenue rose 10% YoY in Q1 FY27, with biopharmaceuticals up 17% and services down 16%. Group EBITDA was INR902 crore at a 21% margin, and reported net profit before exceptionals was INR145 crore (up 245% YoY) as interest cost fell 23% YoY to INR213 crore. Biosimilars grew 16% to INR2,855 crore, while generics grew 21% to INR760 crore with EBITDA margin recovering to 7%. Management said the second half should be stronger, driven by new launches (Aflibercept in the US, denosumab in Europe) and insulin capacity from the Malaysia second drug product line. Working capital and net debt rose sequentially on inventory build ahead of the H2 ramp.

segments.name: Biosimilars
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,855 crore (+16% YoY), EBITDA INR728 crore (25% margin, +10% YoY); R&D at 7% of revenue. North America drove growth; management guides to meaningful acceleration in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Generics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR760 crore (+21% YoY); EBITDA INR56 crore at 7% margin. Improvement attributed to product mix, cost take-out, operating leverage and lower R&D; liraglutide contributed only single-digit share this quarter.

segments.name: Services (Syngene)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR736 crore (-16% YoY) on lower offtake from a key biologics client and a forex hedge loss; EBITDA margin 12%. Guidance: H1 revenue decline, single-digit rupee revenue decline for FY27, margins back to mid-20s.

guidance_outlook: Biosimilars: momentum to build through the year with meaningful acceleration in H2 FY27; management expects biosimilar EBITDA margin in the mid-20s, with a 27% FY26 figure normalised to roughly 24-25%.
Generics: new launches expected to scale in subsequent quarters; operating synergies to be quantified from H2 FY27; margin expansion remains a priority with no specific guidance.
Syngene: FY27 is a transition year, with single-digit rupee revenue degrowth for the full year and EBITDA margins back to mid-20s; return to profitable growth expected from FY28.
Management aims to launch at least one new product in the US or Europe each year through the end of the decade.
Management said it will not increase US manufacturing capex; it will use partnerships and existing US facilities.
capex_capacity: Malaysia insulin facility: EMA approval received for second drug product line; supplies started, with pick-up expected from Q2 FY27.
Working capital build in Q1 is mostly inventory, made to scale up for H2 biosimilars and generics; biosimilar inventory days (DIO) normalised to about 280-290 from over 400 previously.
Depreciation rising as new launch amortisation and newly capitalised facilities come on stream; no specific cost drag quantified for new US and other units.
demand_pricing: Aflibercept (Yesafili) launched in the US in August 2026, with active contracts being tied up; management expects a strong start building into H2.
Five focus growth products: Aflibercept, denosumab (Bosaya/Aukelso), aspart (Kirsty), ustekinumab and bevacizumab; July-September is the payor negotiation window for the next calendar year.
Insulin glargine US market share grew over the last couple of quarters; insulin aspart (Kirsty) moving from closed-door supply to commercial channels in the US.
Management flagged price erosion and competitive pressure as real in biosimilars, offset by integrated cost structure.
Generics: no change in competitive intensity cited; API:formulation mix about 60:40 this quarter versus historical two-thirds:one-third.

qa_highlights.question: What is the generics base business growth ex-liraglutide, and is competitive intensity rising given lower R&D and only a 2% EBITDA gain QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Kedar Upadhye said there is no notable competitive intensity change; liraglutide is still single-digit contribution and not fully reflected. Opex fell sharply across the three companies from Q4 to Q1 and YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Should biosimilar margins rise versus last year's 27%?
qa_highlights.answer: Kedar Upadhye said to normalise FY26's 27% to about 24-25% because of a Q3 North America product mix; management guides to mid-20s with ramp-up, and did not guide beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk that Syngene's decline drags on Biocon's profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Kiran Mazumdar Shaw said Biopharma is about 83% of the business and Services about 17%, so Syngene's temporary decline should not drive group performance; she also noted the structured equity debt element has been retired.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net debt and working capital rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Kedar Upadhye said the increase is mainly inventory built for H2 scale-up in biosimilars and generics, and that net debt rose on working capital rather than new term loans. Finance cost is down 23% YoY and free cash flow goes first to debt reduction.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of US tariffs and is Biocon expanding US manufacturing capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Matt Erick said the reported tariff remark is not current law, since generics and biosimilars are exempt and legislation would be needed. Kiran Mazumdar Shaw said there will be no new US capex; Biocon will use partnerships and existing US facilities.

qa_highlights.question: What is Biocon's stake in Bicara and any plan to monetise it?
qa_highlights.answer: Kiran Mazumdar Shaw said Bicara is no longer significant, the holding is small, and monetisation is not being contemplated at present.

risks_watch: Syngene: H1 revenue decline from reduced demand from a key biologics client; watch for H2 recovery to mid-20s margin.
Generics margin sustainability (7% EBITDA) as liraglutide and new launches ramp, and whether R&D prioritisation affects growth.
Biosimilar price erosion and competition in the US (Aflibercept ramp, insulin aspart commercial transition) and the H2 acceleration being delivered.
Net debt and working capital: whether inventory build converts to sales and whether debt reduces as promised.
Policy risk: the US tariff announcement, which management says is not law today but is being monitored.
summary.management_tone: Confident on biosimilars and H2 acceleration, but cautious and sometimes deflecting on specifics. Management declined to quantify generics base growth, R&D cost drag, and margin guidance beyond mid-20s, pointing to H2 timing.
key_quotes: Q1 performance was broadly in line with our expectations, and we expect momentum to build progressively through the year with meaningful acceleration in the second half of FY'27.
we are not cutting the muscle, we are cutting the fat wherever required.
So, I think you should read this in a very different way than assuming that every business is equally apportioned.

financial_highlights.change: margin up more than 250 bps QoQ

adds.what: Malaysia insulin facility second drug product line (EMA-approved; supplies started, pick-up from Q2 FY27)

growth.why: Management expects H2 FY27 acceleration in biosimilars, backed by Aflibercept US launch with contracts being tied up, denosumab in Europe, and Malaysia insulin second line supplies from Q2 FY27, while Syngene guides to single-digit rupee revenue decline in FY27 and generics launches scale later.
